chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so a man said to him, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! I enter my toilet, and I have neighbors who have slave girls who sing and strike with the oud. Sometimes I prolong my sitting to listen to them.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not do it.'

The man said, 'By Allah, I do not go to them; it is merely a sound that I hear with my ears.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'For the sake of Allah, have you not heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: Indeed, the hearing and the sight and the heart, all of these will be questioned about?'
He said, 'Yes, by Allah! It is as if I had not heard this verse from the Book of Allah from a non-Arab nor an Arab. I will not return to it, if Allah wills, and I seek forgiveness from Allah.'

He (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Rise and perform ritual bath, and ask whatever comes to your mind, for you were standing upon a great matter. How evil would your state have been had you died upon that. Praise Allah and ask Him for repentance from everything He dislikes, for He does not dislike except every ugliness, and leave the ugliness for its people, for everything has its people.'

key_terms.الْفُؤاد: The heart or inner faculty of perception
key_terms.قَبِيح: Ugliness or that which is displeasing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on listening to music or singing from neighbors in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between casual auditory perception and the spiritual accountability of the 'heart' (fu'ad), using the verse from Surah Al-Isra to elevate listening to music from a minor sensory act to a major sin requiring purification. The Imam’s instruction for ghusl underscores the ritual purity associated with repentance from significant spiritual negligence, while the phrase 'leave the ugly to its people' provides a practical framework for social coexistence without necessarily severing ties with non-Muslim or non-practicing neighbors.
